# kgateway Installation Plan

## Overview

**Project**: kgateway  
**Version**: v2.2.4  
**Namespace**: `kgateway-system` (control plane), `demo` (Envoy data plane)  
**Cluster**: `kind-otel-eval-kgateway`  
**Status**: COMPLETE — all three telemetry signals flowing

kgateway is an Envoy-based API gateway control plane implementing the Kubernetes Gateway API. It auto-provisions Envoy proxy pods as data planes. Telemetry is configured via kgateway CRDs (`ListenerPolicy`, `GatewayParameters`).

---

## Step 1: Install Kubernetes Gateway API CRDs

kgateway v2.2.4 requires Gateway API v1.4.1.

```bash
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
```

> Note: Using v1.2.1 (latest stable at time of install). kgateway v2.2.4 requires at minimum v1.1.x standard channel CRDs.

---

## Step 2: Install kgateway CRDs

```bash
helm install kgateway-crds \
  oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway-crds \
  --version v2.2.4 \
  --namespace kgateway-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --wait
```

---

## Step 3: Install kgateway Control Plane

Values file: `.otel-eval/kgateway/kgateway/values.yaml`

```bash
helm install kgateway \
  oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway \
  --version v2.2.4 \
  --namespace kgateway-system \
  --create-namespace \
  -f .otel-eval/kgateway/kgateway/values.yaml \
  --wait --timeout 5m
```

**Key values** (in `values.yaml`):
- `controller.logLevel: info` — default log level
- `podAnnotations.prometheus.io/scrape: "true"` — already set by default

---

## Step 4: Create a Gateway (Envoy proxy instance)

Deploy a `Gateway` resource in the `demo` namespace so the Envoy proxy is co-located with the test backend.

Manifest: `.otel-eval/kgateway/kgateway/routing/gateway.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: demo-gateway
  namespace: demo
spec:
  gatewayClassName: kgateway
  listeners:
    - name: http
      protocol: HTTP
      port: 8080
```

---

## Step 5: Configure Envoy Stats (Prometheus metrics from data plane)

Create a `GatewayParameters` resource to enable Envoy's Prometheus stats endpoint on the auto-provisioned proxy pod.

Manifest: `.otel-eval/kgateway/kgateway/routing/gateway-parameters.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.kgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: GatewayParameters
metadata:
  name: demo-gateway-params
  namespace: demo
spec:
  kube:
    stats:
      enabled: true
      enableStatsRoute: true
```

Reference this from the Gateway via annotation or `gatewayClassParametersRefs` (or patch the default GatewayParameters).

---

## Step 6: Configure OTel Tracing (Envoy data plane → OTel Collector)

Create a `ListenerPolicy` targeting the Gateway to enable OTLP tracing from Envoy.

A `ReferenceGrant` is needed to allow the `ListenerPolicy` in `demo` namespace to reference the OTel Collector service in `opentelemetry` namespace.

Manifests: `.otel-eval/kgateway/kgateway/routing/tracing-policy.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ReferenceGrant
metadata:
  name: allow-demo-to-opentelemetry
  namespace: opentelemetry
spec:
  from:
    - group: gateway.kgateway.dev
      kind: ListenerPolicy
      namespace: demo
  to:
    - group: ""
      kind: Service
---
apiVersion: gateway.kgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: ListenerPolicy
metadata:
  name: otel-tracing
  namespace: demo
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: Gateway
      name: demo-gateway
  default:
    httpSettings:
      tracing:
        provider:
          openTelemetry:
            grpcService:
              backendRef:
                group: ""
                kind: Service
                name: otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector
                namespace: opentelemetry
                port: 4317
            serviceName: "kgateway-envoy.demo"
        randomSampling: 100
        overallSampling: 100
```

---

## Step 7: Configure OTel Access Logs (Envoy data plane → OTel Collector)

Extend the `ListenerPolicy` to also send access logs via OTLP to the collector.

```yaml
      accessLog:
        - openTelemetry:
            grpcService:
              backendRef:
                group: ""
                kind: Service
                name: otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector
                namespace: opentelemetry
                port: 4317
              logName: "envoy-access-log"
```

---

## Step 8: Route Traffic to the Test Backend

Create an `HTTPRoute` to route requests through the Envoy gateway to `otel-eval-backend`.

Manifest: `.otel-eval/kgateway/kgateway/routing/httproute.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: demo-route
  namespace: demo
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: demo-gateway
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: otel-eval-backend
          port: 3000
```

---

## Step 9: Update OTel Collector for Prometheus Scraping

Update the collector's Helm values to scrape:
1. **kgateway controller** metrics at port `9092` in `kgateway-system`
2. **Envoy proxy** stats at port `9901` in `demo`

File: `.otel-eval/kgateway/collector/values.yaml` — add `prometheus` receiver with scrape configs.

```bash
helm upgrade otel-collector open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector \
  --namespace opentelemetry \
  -f .otel-eval/kgateway/collector/values.yaml \
  --wait
```

---

## Step 10: Generate Traffic

```bash
# Port-forward to the Envoy gateway service
kubectl port-forward -n demo svc/demo-gateway 8080:8080 &

# Send traffic (no trace context — Envoy starts new traces)
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  curl -s http://localhost:8080/ | jq .
done

# Send traffic with trace context (Envoy propagates)
curl -s -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" \
  http://localhost:8080/ | jq .
```

---

## Telemetry Summary (Actual)

| Signal  | Source                        | Protocol           | Endpoint / Port                           | Status    |
|---------|-------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------------------------------|-----------|
| Traces  | Envoy data plane              | OTLP gRPC          | otel-collector:4317                       | FLOWING   |
| Metrics | kgateway controller           | Prometheus scrape  | kgateway pod:9092/metrics                 | FLOWING   |
| Metrics | Envoy data plane              | Prometheus scrape  | envoy pod:9091/metrics (NOT 9901)         | FLOWING   |
| Logs    | Envoy access logs (OTel ALS)  | OTLP gRPC          | otel-collector:4317                       | FLOWING   |
| Logs    | kgateway controller           | stdout (k8s logs)  | (not pushed to collector — stdout only)   | N/A       |

> **Note**: The kgateway-provisioned Envoy proxy exposes metrics on port **9091** (not Envoy's default 9901). This is configured by kgateway's deployer and annotated automatically on the pod.

---

## Actual Collector Changes Applied

Added a `prometheus` receiver scraping both the controller and Envoy proxy. Applied via:

```bash
helm repo add open-telemetry https://open-telemetry.github.io/opentelemetry-helm-charts
helm upgrade otel-collector open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector \
  --namespace opentelemetry \
  -f .otel-eval/kgateway/collector/values.yaml \
  --wait
```

The prometheus receiver uses Kubernetes SD to discover pods by annotation (`prometheus.io/scrape: "true"`) and label (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name: demo-gateway`). See `collector/values.yaml` for full config.

---

## Key Notes

1. **ReferenceGrant required**: Cross-namespace gRPC references (ListenerPolicy in `demo` → collector Service in `opentelemetry`) require a `ReferenceGrant` in the target namespace.
2. **Envoy metrics port 9091**: kgateway overrides Envoy's default admin port. The stats are at `:9091/metrics` in Prometheus format.
3. **No OTLP metrics**: kgateway and Envoy only expose Prometheus endpoints; no OTLP push for metrics.
4. **spawnUpstreamSpan**: Required to get both ingress and egress spans; defaults to false.
5. **Log body empty**: OTel ALS log records have an empty body by default; access log data is in resource attributes and trace correlation fields.
